title: SFWeather — 94122 Rainy-Season Outlook
description: Bay Area vacation-planner and rain-risk evidence layer for a listener in San Francisco ZIP 94122, built only from committed verified national weather data (NOAA NCEI station USW00023272, GSOD 72494023234, ISD hourly 72494023234, plus NOAA Storm Events, which holds 119 San Francisco County records of which 99 are rain-related and whose damage column is recorded as unusable). The analysis window runs 2026-10-01 to 2027-01-31, a 123-day season with 6 cost drivers and 5 inputs, generated 2026-09-24T12:49:02Z. Across the 30-year seasonal summary the mean seasonal rainfall is 12.79 inches (median 13.26, range 1.71 to 22.82), the mean number of wet days at or above 0.01 inch is 34.5 (median 35.0, range 7.0 to 55.0 out of 123), and a run of 3 or more consecutive wet days occurs in 96.7% of the 30 seasons — 80.0% for a run of 5 or more, 53.3% for 7 or more, 23.3% for 10 or more, with the longest run averaging 7.3 days and reaching 17.0. Days at or above 0.25 inch average 14.97 and days at or above 1.00 inch average 3.19, against NOAA's published 14.9 and 3.26 — an agreement within 0.06 day. The season is classified El Niño: 11 of the 30 seasons on record were, and the probability of a 7-day-or-longer wet spell there is 81.8%. Executed here: tests/test_parsers.py reports 502 of 502 checks passed, and pipeline/verify_claims.py reports 90 checks passed with 0 failed and 1 documentation-date warning. At this head the scheduled refresh refused to publish because its claim ledger failed, so the committed data below is the last verified state rather than a fresh read.

A smoke test now fails any page text that calls it an upper bound. Session 14 also added an ENSO-phase-conditioned severity table (11 El Nino seasons averaging 3.7 days at 1.00 in or more against 3.2 over all 30, and 3.2 days with a gust of 40 kt or more against 2.4), with every row printing its own n, median and worst season beside the all-season figures, labelled observed rather than forecast.
